core.title: RED tests assert behaviour, not existence
core.given: A test artifact whose declared phase is RED
core.when: any test case exists in it (authored, changed, or checked)
core.then: Every case MUST contain at least one behavioural assertion — on what the code does, the one that fails before the implementation exists — not only existence checks (the stack's vacuous matchers, per profile), and never no assertion.
prefer: Build the case from the bound acceptance, not the code you expect to write: pick the one behaviour it proves; derive the expected outcome from its Then.
Honor declared harness/execution context; enter through the narrowest boundary that still proves the behaviour.
Turn the When into one primary action; create only the Given state it needs.
Assert the observable consequence named (exact error, status/body, state change, emitted item, other declared outcome) — a witness that turns red if the behaviour is removed, inverted or stubbed.
avoid: Existence-only assertions (the stack's vacuous matchers) as the behavioural proof.
Inventing a convenient assertion from the current implementation.
Moving inward to an easier seam that stops exercising what the acceptance claims.
Mocking/substituting the subject or collaboration being proved.
Asserting incidental implementation details instead of the declared outcome.
Computing the expected value with the production code, or copying its algorithm into the test.
Adding an unrelated behavioural assertion merely to clear the automated check.
Broadening one case to prove several unrelated behaviours.
unless: Declared phase is not RED — only RED-phase test artifacts are scanned.
No declared phase — skipped; that is the stack's phase-declaration rule's finding.
Check only: a case mixing existence and behavioural assertions is not flagged (the semantic obligation still applies).
core.why: RED must build the smallest executable proof of the declared acceptance before implementation; an existence check passes once a stub is exported, leaving the acceptance unproven.
evidence: The stack's discipline check reports no finding for RED-phase test artifacts: every case contains at least one behavioural (non-existence) assertion.
Run the target case against the current implementation and confirm execution reaches the intended stimulus and behavioural oracle.
Confirm the behavioural expectation is red because the required behaviour is absent or wrong — not because of syntax, imports, fixture setup, unavailable infrastructure, or an unrelated exception.
Counterfactual check: if the acceptance behaviour disappeared, was inverted, or was replaced by a stub, would this case definitely turn red?
Reviewer checks the asserted expected value traces to the acceptance's Then, is not computed by the production subject, and does not assert on a mock replacing the behaviour being proved.
verification: Machine check (validator): for each test case in a RED-phase test artifact — cases and assertions recognized through the profile's test-case and test-assertion idioms — report a finding when the case contains no assertion at all, or when every assertion uses an existence-only (vacuous) matcher; the stack's vacuous-matcher list comes from the profile (idiom.vacuous_matchers).

The check is deliberately narrower than the semantic obligation: it reports only when every assertion in a case is vacuous. A case that checks existence and then behaviour is not reported, because the behavioural assertion is the machine-visible proxy; a non-finding therefore does not exempt the case from the semantic obligation.

Check blind spots, judged semantically (reviewer or LLM): expected values computed by the production subject, assertions on mocks replacing the behaviour being proved, and unrelated assertions added only to satisfy the check all produce structurally acceptable cases that prove the wrong thing.

Scope: only test artifacts whose declared phase is RED are scanned; artifacts with no declared phase are skipped and belong to the stack's phase-declaration rule. The check scans every case in such artifacts, not only edited ones.
Severity 3; disposition strict — every finding fails the check run; no advisory mode and no ratchet baseline.

fires: Check finding: a RED-phase case whose only assertion is an existence check (e.g. asserting the subject exists / is defined).
Check finding: a RED-phase case whose assertions are all existence checks (the stack's vacuous matchers).
Check finding: a RED-phase case containing no assertion at all.
Semantic applicability: any RED-phase case — existing, new or changed, flagged or not — including cases mixing existence and behavioural assertions, which must still carry a real behavioural witness.
doesNotFire: Rule not applicable: a test artifact whose declared phase is GREEN or REFACTOR.
Rule not applicable here: a test artifact with no declared phase (that is the stack's phase-declaration rule's finding).
Check non-finding only (semantic rule still applies): a RED case that checks existence and also makes a behavioural assertion.

profileRequirements.meaning: The stack's test runner/framework under whose constructs test artifacts are written; it identifies which artifacts are test artifacts and pairs with the case/assertion idioms below to instantiate the core's 'test artifact', 'test case' and 'assertion' recognition.
profileRequirements.bunValue: bun:test — Bun's built-in test runner; test files are those using `bun:test` it()/expect() matchers

profileRequirements.meaning: What one test case looks like in a test artifact — the construct that delimits a single case and its body; the obligation and the check apply per case.
profileRequirements.bunValue: `it()` — each `it()` in the test file is one case

profileRequirements.meaning: What an assertion looks like in a test artifact — the construct the check counts as one assertion when deciding 'no assertion at all' vs 'every assertion vacuous'.
profileRequirements.bunValue: `expect(` calls — a case's assertions are its `expect(` calls applying matchers

profileRequirements.meaning: The stack's existence-only (vacuous) assertion matchers — assertions that pass the moment a stub is exported; the core's 'existence check' is instantiated with this list.
The syntax by which a test case binds itself to the acceptance it proves; the core's 'bound acceptance' in prefer[0] refers to it.

proposedKeys.meaning: What one test case looks like in a test artifact — the construct that delimits a single case and its body; instantiates the core's per-case obligation ('every test case') and the check's per-case scan.
proposedKeys.bunValue: `it()` — each `it()` in the test file is one case
proposedKeys.whyNoExistingKey: The idiom group covers boundary, auth, error, validation, import, nesting, naming, markup and request-gate idioms only; no key describes test-case structure, so a stack-neutral core cannot otherwise say what counts as one case.

proposedKeys.meaning: What an assertion looks like in a test artifact — the construct counted as one assertion when deciding 'no assertion at all' versus 'every assertion vacuous'.
proposedKeys.bunValue: `expect(` calls — a case's assertions are its `expect(` calls applying matchers
proposedKeys.whyNoExistingKey: Same gap in the idiom group: no key describes the test-assertion construct, so 'contains at least one behavioural assertion' cannot be instantiated per stack.

proposedKeys.meaning: The stack's existence-only (vacuous) assertion matchers — assertions that pass the moment a stub is exported; instantiates the core's 'existence check'.
proposedKeys.whyNoExistingKey: The idiom group covers boundary, markup, control-flow and naming idioms only; no key describes the test-assertion vocabulary, so the core's 'existence check' cannot otherwise be instantiated per stack.

neutralityNotes: The obligation itself is stack-neutral; only its instantiation is stack-specific. (1) Test recognition is profile data: the runner/framework uses the existing key tooling.test_runner, and the case/assertion constructs are proposed as idiom.test_case and idiom.test_assertion (no existing idiom key covers test structure); the vacuous-matcher list is proposed as idiom.vacuous_matchers; the acceptance-binding syntax already exists as urn.binding.acceptance (@covers). (2) The language fact (typescript/javascript over bun:test files) is a realization-only scan gate: per feedback, tooling.languages means languages of production source, and the neutral core does not need test-language data, so the gate stays in the Bun realization rather than in the profile. (3) Phase-declaration syntax is owned by the stack's phase-declaration rule and is not profiled here; the core consumes the declared phase as an observable fact and skips artifacts with none. (4) Detector/validator ids, the brace-matching parsing mechanics, sibling Bun rule ids, and the strict-disposition policy node have no neutral equivalent and stay bunOnly; the core's verification describes the check generically and carries severity 3 + strict disposition itself (per PLT-84 these are not profile keys). (5) splitSuggestion, audit, trace, additions and sharedNodes are sidecar metadata, not agent-facing items, so they fall outside item classification; the concrete reference example in prefer[3] is delivered only through bun.json.
